recommendation: Keep this commit. It removes the remaining source-level contradiction for FHIR-38735 while preserving the later applied FHIR-52878 regex behavior; any future decision to make the regex require timezone whenever a time is present should be handled as a separate work-group issue.
issue_request: FHIR-38735 was a Published/Persuasive R5 technical correction reporting that the dateTime regex rejected date-only values such as 1990-01-01 unless a timezone suffix was present. The final Jira comment confirmed that timezone is only permitted when a full time is specified and that the earlier attachment's regex direction should be used.
initial_application: Commit c5ab3c3dec1d1498d8ea238a596046692a38c501 applied the issue by changing source/datatypes/primitives.xml so date-only and partial-date values no longer required a timezone suffix. That application left the dateTime row Comments cell saying UTC offset was allowed for dates and partial dates.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes for January 2023 record FHIR-38735 first as a technical correction needing the correct regex and then as auto-approved. Later Applied/Persuasive issue FHIR-52878 and commit 65790c792003e57c5c12a0b1243f4539922fa008 moved timezone syntax inside the time branch of the dateTime regex. The related Zulip discussion says the regex need not enforce every rule, so this reconciliation preserves the later-approved regex while fixing the stale source comment.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes/primitives.xml so the dateTime Comments cell says UTC offset is allowed only when a time is specified. No regex change was made because the current regex already accepts date-only values and rejects offsets on date-only values after FHIR-52878.
source_changes: source/datatypes/primitives.xml: changed the dateTime primitive Comments cell from 'UTC offset is allowed for dates and partial dates' to 'UTC offset is allowed only when a time is specified'.

related_jiras.note: Applied/Persuasive R6 clarification that tightened the dateTime regex so timezone offsets only appear with a time component, while noting regexes need not enforce every rule.
